title: Plaint thrown out, suit goes to trial

scenes.dialogue: You pay an advance on a handwritten deal for farmland, and the sellers then sell it to others. Can a court throw out your suit before any trial even begins?
In Andhra Pradesh, a trial court did just that, mainly calling the deal a mere agreement to agree. The buyer appealed to the High Court. Was the deal incomplete?
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On third November, Honourable Justice D Ramesh and Honourable Justice Alapati Giridhar ruled.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On 3 November, Honourable Justice D. Ramesh and Honourable Justice Alapati Giridhar ruled.

scenes.dialogue: The deal, written in January twenty ten, covered forty seven and a half acres for two crore thirty eight lakh rupees. The buyer paid five lakh as advance.
scenes.shown: The deal, written in January 2010, covered 47.5 acres for ₹2.38 crore. The buyer paid ₹5 lakh as advance.

scenes.dialogue: One owner wrote and signed it by hand, for her whole family, the buyer says. That August, the owners sold the land to others, and he sued for specific performance.
All the defendants sought rejection of the plaint. The paper, they said, named no buyer or seller, described no property, and only promised a later agreement.
They also said she had no authority to sign for the other owners. The buyer replied that she never denied her handwriting or the five lakh advance.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? At this stage, only the plaint and its documents count, and on its face, this paper had every essential term of a sale.
The disputed points must go to trial. The appeals were allowed with costs, and the buyer must deposit the balance sale price within ten days, in fixed deposits.
